error_not_found: The requested item does not exist.
error_database_unavailable: The database is not reachable. Please try again later.
error_internal: Something went wrong on the server.
error_invalid_credentials: User name or password is wrong.
error_account_locked: This account is locked out. Try again later or ask an administrator.
error_password_change_required: The password must be changed first, for example when signing in to Windows.
error_too_many_attempts: Too many failed sign-ins. Please wait a few minutes.
error_forbidden_origin: The request came from another website and was blocked.
error_directory_unavailable: The directory (Active Directory) is not reachable.
vault_intro: Encrypted in your browser. Only you can read it.
vault_setup_hint: Choose a passphrase. Nobody can reset it for you: without the passphrase, a passkey or the recovery key, the entries are lost.
vault_recovery_hint: Write it down or print it, and keep it apart from the passphrase. It is shown only now.
vault_wrong: That does not unlock the vault.
vault_unreadable: This entry does not open with this vault's key.
vault_recovered_hint: An administrator recovered this vault. Keep this new recovery key, then choose a new passphrase.
vault_prf_unsupported: This passkey cannot derive keys (WebAuthn PRF). Use another one, e.g. a recent security key or your device's passkeys.
vault_reset_confirm: This deletes every entry and every way to unlock the vault. Nobody can bring them back.
audit_verify_ok: The log is intact: {entries} entries checked.
audit_verify_broken: The log was changed from entry {seq} on.
error_forbidden: You are not permitted to do this.
break_glass_intro: For when the directory is unavailable. Every sign-in here is recorded.
break_glass_banner: Signed in with an emergency account. Everything you do is recorded.
error_name_taken: This name is already used here.
error_folder_not_empty: The folder is not empty. Move or delete its contents first.
catalog_select_hint: Select a device, a credential or a folder.
field_password_keep: Leave empty to keep the current password.
auth_device_target_changed: Another target, or another kind, needs the password or key again.
auth_certificate: A certificate from remotehub, as myself
auth_laps_hint: Read from the directory at every connection.
auth_certificate_hint: remotehub signs a key for your user name, valid for minutes. The device's sshd must trust remotehub's certificate authority (TrustedUserCAKeys), whose public key is at {url}
requests_none_mine: You have not asked for access yet.
terminal_pinned: First connection: the host key {fingerprint} is now pinned.
terminal_credentials_hint: Used for this connection only and never stored.
terminal_host_key_changed: The host key of {name} changed: pinned {expected}, now {presented}. This happens when a device is reinstalled — or when someone intercepts the connection.
error_own_account_unavailable: Your sign-in password is not available in this session. Sign in again — or this is switched off here.
error_ssh_ca_unavailable: remotehub has no SSH certificate authority set up, so it cannot issue a certificate.
error_laps_unavailable: The directory holds no LAPS password for this device that remotehub may read.
error_last_unlock: The last way to unlock the vault cannot be removed.
error_vault_not_covered: This vault is not wrapped for the organisation recovery key yet. It will be at its next unlock.
error_recovery_key_in_use: Vaults still depend on this recovery key.
error_recovery_open: A recovery of this vault is open already.
error_recovery_not_ready: The recovery is not approved, or its day has passed.
error_request_pending: The same request is already waiting for a decision.
error_request_decided: This request has been decided already.
field_key_keep: Leave empty to keep the current key, passphrase and certificate.
error_field_private_key: This is not a private key in OpenSSH or PEM format.
error_field_passphrase: The key's passphrase is missing or wrong.
error_field_certificate: The certificate is not an OpenSSH user certificate for this key.
display_label: Remote desktop of {name} — click into it to type
display_failed_target: The device could not be reached, refused the sign-in or presented an unexpected certificate.
display_ended: The session was ended on the device.
credentials_username_optional: User name (if the device asks for one)
keyboard_layout_unicode: Unicode (any layout, some shortcuts may not work)
error_tls_required: The device offers Remote Desktop only without TLS; remotehub does not connect to it unencrypted.
audit_personal_unlock_added: Added a way to unlock the personal vault
audit_personal_unlock_removed: Removed a way to unlock the personal vault
display_certificate_pinned: First connection: the certificate {fingerprint} is now pinned.
display_certificate_changed: The certificate of {name} changed: pinned {expected}, now {presented}. This happens when a certificate is renewed — or when someone intercepts the connection.
connectors_token_hint: Shown this once, and kept nowhere. Give the connector these settings:
connectors_token_docs: How to start it: docs/install.md, section Reach devices in other networks.
error_connector_in_use: Devices are still reached through this connector.
error_connector_offline: The device's connector is not connected.
error_purpose_required: State the purpose of the connection.
error_accounts_unavailable: The service for local accounts is not reachable.
error_second_factor_required: Confirm the sign-in with the second factor.
error_second_factor_setup_required: Set up a second factor first.
kratos_provider_not_linked: No account is linked to this sign-in. Sign in with the password once and link it under My account.
sign_in_second_hint: Enter the code from your authenticator app.
sign_in_recovery_hint: Enter one of your recovery codes. Each works once.
kratos_expired: This took too long. Please start again.
kratos_code_invalid: The code is not right. Please try again.
kratos_recovery_code_invalid: The code is not right, or was used already.
recovery_email_hint: Enter the address of your account. A code to set a new password goes there.
recovery_code_hint: Enter the code from your invitation or the e-mail.
setup_password_hint: Choose a password of at least 12 characters.
setup_totp_hint: remotehub asks for a second factor at every sign-in. Set up an authenticator app.
account_not_local: This account is managed in the directory.
account_totp_active: Set up. Every sign-in asks for its code.
account_totp_hint: Scan the code with an authenticator app, or enter the key by hand. Then enter the code the app shows.
account_totp_qr: QR code for the authenticator app
account_codes_hint: For when the authenticator app is not at hand. Each code works once.
account_providers_hint: A linked account signs you in instead of the password. The second factor is still asked for.
vault_unlock_to_use: Unlock my vault to use its entries
purpose_hint: It goes into the device's journal.
recovery_intro: Personal vaults are also wrapped for the organisation recovery key. With its private key, an administrator can recover a vault once a security officer has approved it. The private key never reaches the server.
recovery_no_key: There is no recovery key yet. Without one, no personal vault can be recovered.
recovery_key_create_hint: The private key is made in this browser. It is handed out twice: as a file sealed with this passphrase, and as text to print and keep in a safe. The server keeps only the public key.
recovery_key_shown_once: The key file was downloaded. Print this text and keep it in a safe. It is shown only now.
recovery_no_vaults: Nobody has set up a personal vault yet.
recovery_covered_older: Covered by an older key until the next unlock
recovery_not_covered: Not covered until the next unlock
recovery_kind_passphrase: Forgotten passphrase: a one-time recovery key for the owner
recovery_kind_handover: Hand-over: the entries go into a shared folder
recovery_key_unreadable: That is not a private key, or the passphrase is wrong.
recovery_key_wrong: This private key does not open the vault.
recovery_one_time_hint: Give this one-time recovery key to {name}. It unlocks the vault once; then a new passphrase and recovery key are due.
purpose_rules_hint: These users and groups state a purpose before every connection. It goes into the device's journal and the audit log.
users_hint: Everyone who has signed in, and the local accounts invited so far.
users_block_confirm: Block {name}? Their sessions end now, and they cannot sign in until you unblock them.
users_end_sessions_confirm: End every session of {name}? They can sign in again.
users_recovery_confirm: Give {name} a new sign-in code? Their authenticator app stops working and their sessions end; with the code, they set a new password and second factor.
users_delete_confirm: Delete the account of {name}? This cannot be undone. The audit log keeps its entries.
users_invite_hint: Creates a local account. Hand its owner the link and the code; with them, they set a password and an authenticator app.
users_code_hint: Hand these to the account's owner. They are shown only now.
audit_account_recovery_issued: Issued a sign-in code for a local account
groups_hint: Groups of remotehub's own. Grant access to them like to directory groups; their members are users and directory groups.
groups_delete_confirm: Delete the group {name}? The permissions and purpose rules given to it go with it.
audit_group_member_added: Added a member to a group
audit_group_member_removed: Removed a member from a group
roles_hint: Roles for remotehub itself, given to users and groups. The administrators set at installation keep their role and are not listed here.
role_administrator_hint: Manages everything: devices, permissions, users and settings.
role_auditor_hint: Reads and checks the audit log.
audit_session_ended_by_directory: The directory ended a user's sessions
error_second_factor_invalid: The code is not right. Please try again.
factor_setup_required: Your account needs an authenticator app.
factor_setup_hint: Add it to your authenticator app with this key, then enter the code the app shows.
factor_none: Not set up. With an app, every sign-in asks for its code as well.
factor_required_here: Your account needs it: it stays.
factor_rules_hint: These users and groups set up an authenticator app at their next sign-in, and use it at every sign-in after. Local accounts always have one.
users_reset_factor_confirm: Remove the authenticator app of {name}, e.g. after a lost phone? If their account needs one, they set up a new one at the next sign-in.
audit_second_factor_waived: No longer asked for a second factor
reveal_copied: Copied. It leaves the clipboard in {seconds} seconds.
reveal_copy_failed: The browser did not let remotehub use the clipboard.
audit_credential_revealed: Showed or copied a stored credential
vault_shared_hint: Credentials of the folders you may see. With the right to reveal them, you show or copy them here too; each time is recorded.
kdbx_new_password: Master password of the new file
kdbx_export_hint: The file holds every password in plain sight of whoever opens it with this master password. Keep it as safe as the vault.
kdbx_unreadable: The file does not open with this password, or it is no KeePass file.
kdbx_missing_reveal: An export takes the right to reveal everything in the folder, which {name} lacks.
vault_file_too_large: Files may have up to {megabytes} MB.
audit_credential_attachment_added: Added a file to a credential
audit_credential_attachment_deleted: Removed a file of a credential
audit_personal_attachment_saved: Saved a file of the personal vault
audit_personal_attachment_deleted: Deleted a file of the personal vault
